title: Chronic PPDs/6PPDQ exposure triggers lung injury via MDM2 binding-mediated p53 accumulation and PI3K-AKT signaling repression.
authors: Zhao, Chao; Zhang, Jing; Wang, Xin; Dong, Ruijun; Xu, Xin; Sun, Shuting; Guo, Ziwei; Cai, Zicong; Yin, Dingxiao; Wang, Qianqian; Zhang, Hu
one_liner_zh: 该文研究环境污染物PPDs/6PPDQ通过MDM2-p53结合诱导肺损伤，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白结合与分子对接，但核心是毒理学机制而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: P-phenylenediamines (PPDs) and their quinone derivatives (PPDQs) are widely employed as antioxidants in the manufacturing of rubber products. Their pervasive environmental distribution has led to widespread human exposure, raising concerns about respiratory health. While pulmonary toxicity has been reported, the molecular mechanisms underlying lung injury induced by chronic low-dose co-exposure to multiple PPDs/PPDQs congeners remain unclear. Here, we selected five environmentally prevalent PPDs (6PPD, 77PD, CPPD, DPPD, and IPPD) alongside 6PPDQ, and integrated network toxicology, molecular docking, in vivo and in vitro experiments, and transcriptomic profiling to investigate the common molecular targets and signaling pathways. Our findings demonstrated that PPDs/6PPDQ bound to the p53-binding domain of MDM2, thereby blocking MDM2-mediated p53 degradation and resulting in persistent p53 protein accumulation. Under chronic stress, sustained p53 elevation was functionally associated with downregulation of the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway, which drove cellular senescence and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), promoted a pro-inflammatory microenvironment, and ultimately disrupted pulmonary epithelial barrier integrity. Despite limited overlap at the gene level, both network toxicology and transcriptomic analyses converged on the PI3K-AKT pathway as the key signaling axis. This study revealed the core regulatory role of the MDM2-p53 axis and its crosstalk with the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway in PPDs/6PPDQ-induced lung injury, providing new mechanistic insights for the prevention and intervention of respiratory diseases associated with environmental pollutants.
abstract_zh: 对苯二胺类化合物（PPDs）及其醌类衍生物（PPDQs）广泛用作橡胶制品制造中的抗氧化剂。其普遍的环境分布导致人群广泛暴露，引发对呼吸系统健康的担忧。尽管已有肺毒性报道，但慢性低剂量共同暴露于多种PPDs/PPDQs同系物诱导肺损伤的分子机制仍不清楚。本研究选取了五种环境中普遍存在的PPDs（6PPD、77PD、CPPD、DPPD和IPPD）以及6PPDQ，并整合网络毒理学、分子对接、体内和体外实验及转录组分析，以探究共同的分子靶点和信号通路。研究结果表明，PPDs/6PPDQ与MDM2的p53结合域结合，从而阻断MDM2介导的p53降解，导致p53蛋白持续积累。在慢性应激下，持续的p53升高在功能上与PI3K-AKT信号通路下调相关，进而驱动细胞衰老和衰老相关分泌表型（SASP），促进促炎微环境，最终破坏肺上皮屏障完整性。尽管在基因水平上重叠有限，但网络毒理学和转录组分析均聚焦于PI3K-AKT通路作为关键信号轴。本研究揭示了MDM2-p53轴及其与PI3K-AKT信号通路串扰在PPDs/6PPDQ诱导肺损伤中的核心调控作用，为环境污染物相关呼吸系统疾病的预防和干预提供了新的机制见解。
